narrativeReportMd:
# Resource R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`Resource` keeps the same canonical identity and the same local element set, cardinalities, element names, and wire representation. One hard validation break was found: `Resource.language` changes from a preferred Common Languages binding to a required All Languages binding, so R4 instances with non-BCP-47 language codes can become invalid in R6.

## Scope
The report is scoped to the abstract base `Resource` artifact. Because this is the Resource report, the explicit R6 `Base` superclass is treated locally. Changes in dependent datatypes, profiles, search parameters, operations, terminology-server expansion behavior, and the `additionalImplicitRules` extension are out of scope.

## Main migration themes
The major migration theme is stricter base-resource conformance for `Resource.language`. Tooling should also account for R6 model metadata changes: `Resource` now has an explicit `Base` superclass and `Resource.id` carries a FHIR type marker of `id` rather than `string` while retaining the same FHIRPath string representation.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact finding is `Resource:TERMINOLOGY_BINDING:Resource.language:binding-strength`, because it can turn previously acceptable R4 resource instances into R6 validation errors. The class-hierarchy and `Resource.id` type-marker changes are mainly runtime/code-generation risks rather than wire-format breaks.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most useful for the BCP-47 terminology behavior and for generated-code/library impacts of the `Resource.id` marker change. The package evidence clearly shows the structural deltas, but exact implementation impact depends on validators, terminology servers, and code generators.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The stricter language binding could have been introduced less disruptively through profiles or warnings, but a required all-BCP-47 binding is a defensible base-specification cleanup. The explicit `Base` superclass and `id` marker correction are also likely justified infrastructure clarifications, with compatibility shims needed for older generators.

## Follow-up analysis
Follow-up should cover live BCP-47 terminology validation, generated model behavior for `Base` and `id`, and the separately defined `additionalImplicitRules` extension.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `Resource` has one clear local hard validation break: `Resource.language` now requires membership in the All Languages BCP-47 value set. The main migration concerns are stricter language validation, generator handling of the new `Base` superclass, and generator handling of `Resource.id` as `id` rather than generic `string`. Confidence is high for the computable deltas and lower only for exact terminology-server behavior and downstream library impact.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should focus first on validating and normalizing base `language` values across all resource types, especially common legacy values such as underscore-separated locale tags. Code generators and validators should then be checked for assumptions that R4 `Resource` has no declared superclass or that `Resource.id` is a generic string marker. No local element additions, removals, renames, or cardinality changes require data-shape transforms.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high because both assigned StructureDefinitions are present at the expected canonical URL and the local snapshot/differential deltas are small and direct. Confidence for the `Resource.language` validation mechanism is high at the binding-strength level, but exact accepted BCP-47 tag behavior depends on terminology-server implementation. Confidence for runtime/code-generation impact is medium because it depends on how individual tools consume `baseDefinition`, `derivation`, and the `structuredefinition-fhir-type` extension.

findings.title: Resource now explicitly specializes Base

oldState.summary: R4 Resource has stable canonical identity but no declared baseDefinition or derivation.
oldState.narrativeMd: In the R4 package, `StructureDefinition/Resource` is the abstract base resource type and does not declare `baseDefinition` or `derivation`.

newState.summary: R6 Resource retains identity but declares baseDefinition Base and derivation specialization.
newState.narrativeMd: In the R6 ballot package, `StructureDefinition/Resource` still has the same canonical URL and remains abstract, but now declares `baseDefinition = http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/Base` and `derivation = specialization`.

facts.note: The R6 Base snapshot has only the root Base element and no local instance fields.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The artifact was matched by identical canonical URL, id, name, kind, and type. The change is a root metadata/class-hierarchy delta, not a rename or replacement.

impact.impactRationaleMd: No Resource instance element is added, removed, renamed, or made mandatory. Existing JSON/XML resources do not need a new field for `Base`. The risk is in validators, differential processors, and generated model hierarchies that assumed `Resource` had no superclass or that treated a missing `baseDefinition` as the root condition.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: This is infrastructure-level risk. It can block deployments if toolchains fail, but it does not by itself alter clinical content.

justification.inferredGoal: Unify all FHIR resources and types under an explicit abstract Base node in the R6 type system.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `Resource` as the formal root and describe `Base` as narrative or auxiliary tooling metadata instead of a computable superclass.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: R6 makes the common FHIR type-system root explicit by declaring `Resource` as a specialization of `Base`. This does not change instance content, but it can break generators, validators, and hierarchy walkers that treated absence of `baseDefinition` as the root condition. A less-breaking design exists only in a partial sense because keeping `Base` outside the formal derivation chain would preserve old tooling assumptions while leaving the R6 hierarchy less computable and less uniform.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would leave `Resource.baseDefinition` absent and publish `Base` as conceptual documentation or auxiliary tooling metadata. That preserves most existing R4 code-generation assumptions, but it fails the strongest version of the R6 goal: a formal `Base` -> `Resource` derivation in the core StructureDefinitions. Because the alternative is incomplete rather than an equivalent low-cost design, the break is probably justified.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 hierarchy assumptions for older generators, but does not fully meet the R6 goal of a formal, uniform `Base` to `Resource` type model.

evidence.detail: R4 Resource has no `baseDefinition` or `derivation` property.
R6 Resource declares `baseDefinition` as Base and `derivation` as specialization.
R6 Base is an abstract complex type with a single root element and no local child elements.

examples.examplesMd: No instance JSON example is provided because the wire instance shape is unchanged; the issue is generated hierarchy and StructureDefinition processing.

findings.narrativeMd: `Resource` now sits under an explicit `Base` StructureDefinition. This is not a data migration problem, but it can surprise tools that special-cased `Resource` as the root of the computable hierarchy or used absence of `baseDefinition` to detect the root.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid resource instance does not become invalid merely because `Resource` now specializes `Base`. R6-to-R4 instance representation is also unaffected. The compatibility concern is runtime/tooling: loaders, code generators, inheritance walkers, and differential validators need to handle `Base` before `Resource`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update model generators and validators to treat `Base` as the R6 root and `Resource` as a specialization. Regression tests should include loading `StructureDefinition-Base.json`, walking from a concrete resource to `Resource` to `Base`, and ensuring no extra instance members are generated from `Base`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change was probably made to make the FHIR type system more explicit and uniform. A compatibility-preserving alternative would have left `Resource.baseDefinition` absent and exposed `Base` only as explanatory metadata, but that would perpetuate special cases in the R6 model.

findings.title: Resource.id FHIR type marker changed from string to id

oldState.summary: R4 Resource.id is 0..1 and has type code FHIRPath System.String with fhir-type marker `string`.

semanticText.definition: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.
semanticText.comment: The only time that a resource does not have an id is when it is being submitted to the server using a create operation.

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 ElementDefinition uses the FHIRPath string type code and a `structuredefinition-fhir-type` extension value of `string`.

newState.summary: R6 Resource.id is still 0..1 and still represented as FHIRPath System.String, but the fhir-type marker is `id`.

semanticText.definition: The logical id of the resource, as used in the URL for the resource. Once assigned, this value never changes.
semanticText.comment: Within the context of the FHIR RESTful interactions, the resource has an id except for cases like the create and conditional update. Otherwise, the use of the resouce id depends on the given use case.

newState.narrativeMd: The R6 ElementDefinition keeps the same cardinality and FHIRPath string representation but changes the `structuredefinition-fhir-type` extension value to `id`.

facts.note: The low-level FHIRPath representation is unchanged.

facts.oldValue: The only time that a resource does not have an id is when it is being submitted to the server using a create operation.
facts.newValue: Within RESTful interactions, id is absent for cases like create and conditional update; otherwise use depends on the use case.
facts.note: Comment wording broadened; this is not the primary compatibility concern.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element is matched by identical ElementDefinition id and path `Resource.id`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The wire representation remains a JSON/XML string, so ordinary instances do not change shape. The risk is for generators and validators that consumed the R4 `fhir-type` marker as generic `string` and will now generate or enforce the narrower primitive `id`. If an implementation accepted non-id-shaped logical ids because of the R4 marker, R6 validation or typed APIs can reject them.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect logical id handling can break REST routing, reference resolution, or persistence keys, but this does not directly change clinical meaning.

justification.inferredGoal: Align the computable type marker for `Resource.id` with the intended FHIR `id` primitive.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the computable marker as `string` while adding a warning-level id constraint or separate compatibility annotation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable because `Resource.id` is a FHIR logical id, and the R6 marker makes that primitive subtype explicit for tools. The wire representation and cardinality remain unchanged, so the break is mostly generated-model and validator churn. A less-breaking design could keep the old `string` marker and add prose, a warning constraint, or an auxiliary annotation, but that would not give generic R6 tooling the same authoritative computable signal that this element is an `id`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would retain the `structuredefinition-fhir-type` value of `string` and add an id-shaped invariant, warning, or additional annotation. If placed in the base definitions this would be more than ordinary migration guidance, but it is only a partial alternative: warning-level rules do not enforce the primitive semantics, while duplicate annotations risk conflicting signals and allow overly broad generated string APIs to persist.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves older generated APIs but either leaves the main primitive marker misleading or creates duplicate metadata that tools may interpret inconsistently.

evidence.detail: R4 `Resource.id` uses FHIRPath System.String with fhir-type extension value `string`.
R6 `Resource.id` uses the same FHIRPath System.String code with fhir-type extension value `id`.

examples.examplesMd: No old-valid/new-invalid example is asserted because the normative R4 intent for logical ids was already `id`-like. The risk is primarily for toolchains that used the package marker to generate a generic string API.

findings.narrativeMd: `Resource.id` did not change its path, cardinality, summary flag, or wire scalar representation. The computable FHIR type hint changed from `string` to `id`, which can affect generated model property types, validation adapters, schema generation, and code that serializes or normalizes ids.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Strict R6 validators or generated setters may now enforce `id` primitive rules where an R4-package-driven tool permitted a generic string. R6 ids remain representable in R4 wire format because both are strings on the wire, but older typed clients may have looser or differently named APIs.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit generated Resource base classes and validation code for the `id` property. Treat the R6 property as the FHIR `id` primitive and normalize legacy ids before migration. Include tests for ordinary ids, missing ids on create, conditional update cases, and invalid strings that contain whitespace or locale-like characters not allowed by an id validator.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 change is likely a correction toward the intended primitive semantics. A compatibility annotation could have eased generator migration, but retaining the generic marker would make every R6 resource continue to expose an overly broad id type.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R4 package evidence conflicts with common human expectations that `Resource.id` is an `id` primitive. Human review should focus on actual validator and code-generator behavior rather than assuming all R4 systems treated it as arbitrary string.

findings.title: Resource.language binding strengthened from preferred Common Languages to required All Languages

oldState.summary: R4 Resource.language is optional code with a preferred binding to Common Languages.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R4 also carries an `elementdefinition-maxValueSet` extension pointing to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/all-languages`, but the primary binding strength is only preferred.

semanticText.definition: The base language in which the resource is written.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, a language code outside the Common Languages value set is not a base validation error from the primary binding because the binding is preferred.

newState.summary: R6 Resource.language is optional code with a required binding to All Languages.

binding.description: IETF language tag for a human language

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The required R6 value set composes all codes from `urn:ietf:bcp:47`. The R6 Common Languages value set is retained only as an additional starter binding.

semanticText.definition: The base language in which the resource is written.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, `Resource.language` must validate as a BCP-47 language tag through the All Languages required value set when the element is present.

facts.newValue: IETF language tag for a human language

facts.note: The R6 primary required binding now points directly to All Languages.
Common Languages remains as a starter set, not as the conformance-limiting primary binding.
Local ValueSet compose comparison found 37 added starter concepts and no removed starter concepts.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element is matched by identical ElementDefinition id and path `Resource.language`; the local element cardinality and type remain unchanged while binding metadata changes.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation-strengthening change. In R4, a non-Common-Languages or malformed language code could pass base validation with at most preferred-binding guidance. In R6, when `Resource.language` is present, it must be in the required All Languages value set, so invalid BCP-47 tags become errors.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Language tags affect indexing, accessibility, generated presentation, and localization. Invalid tags can cause clinical content to be presented or searched under the wrong language assumptions.

justification.inferredGoal: Make base resource language tags conformant to BCP-47 rather than merely recommending common tags.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep a non-required All Languages/BCP-47 base binding with warning-level validation, while strict profiles require valid BCP-47 tags where needed.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: `Resource.language` is the base language for resource content, and a required all-languages binding makes the BCP-47 requirement machine-checkable across all resources. The compatibility cost is real because R4's preferred binding allowed local or malformed language codes to remain base-valid. A softer base binding would be less disruptive, but it would materially weaken the R6 guarantee that present `Resource.language` values are interoperable language tags.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would retain preferred or extensible-style conformance to All Languages, possibly with a base best-practice warning for non-BCP-47 tags and profile-level hard requirements for strict exchanges. That preserves old instances with local or malformed language values. It is only a partial alternative because profile requirements or warning validation are not a substitute for a base R6 rule that all generic validators and receivers can rely on.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves legacy local or malformed R4 language values, but does not guarantee interoperable BCP-47 language tags in every base R6 resource.

evidence.detail: R4 binding strength is preferred and the primary value set is Common Languages.
R4 also includes a max value set extension for All Languages, but this is not the primary preferred binding.
R6 binding strength is required and the primary value set is versioned All Languages.
R6 All Languages includes codes from `urn:ietf:bcp:47`.
The R6 Common Languages starter value set locally has 93 concepts, 37 more than R4 and none removed in the local compose comparison.

examples.examplesMd: The example uses `Patient` only to show a concrete resource carrying inherited `Resource.language`. `en_US` is illustrative of a common non-BCP-47 locale spelling; migration should normalize it to the BCP-47 form `en-US` when that is the intended meaning.

findings.narrativeMd: `Resource.language` is still optional and still a `code`, but the conformance rule for present values is much stricter. This matters because `Resource.language` is inherited by all resources: any legacy data that used local language mnemonics, underscore locales, or otherwise invalid tags can fail R6 validation even though it was not a hard R4 base error.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with `language` present and outside the required R6 All Languages value set can become R6-invalid. Valid R6 language values are still representable in R4 as a `code`; an R4 validator might issue preferred-binding advice if a tag is outside the old Common Languages starter set, but representation is not lost.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory all resource instances with `language`. Normalize common legacy spellings such as `en_US` to BCP-47 `en-US`, reject or map local mnemonics, and document any private-use tags. Tests should cover omitted language, valid common tags, valid less-common BCP-47 tags, malformed tags, and underscore locale strings. A terminology service or BCP-47 validator should be used rather than a finite enum generated from Common Languages.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is probably justified because a base language tag should be a real BCP-47 tag. The backward-compatible alternative would have kept a preferred binding and enforced BCP-47 through profiles or warnings, preserving old data at the cost of weaker base interoperability.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: A live terminology expansion was not run. Reviewers should confirm how their R6 terminology server validates BCP-47, including grandfathered, private-use, script, and region subtags.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The local Resource snapshot has the same element ids in R4 and R6: `Resource`, `Resource.id`, `Resource.meta`, `Resource.implicitRules`, and `Resource.language`.
All local cardinalities are unchanged: root `0..*`; `id`, `meta`, `implicitRules`, and `language` each remain `0..1`.
`Resource` has no local `Reference`-typed element, so no reference target change applies.

The local `ele-1` FHIRPath expression, severity, and source remain materially the same on `meta`, `implicitRules`, and `language`. R6 omits the R4 `xpath` property, but that is treated as global ElementDefinition metadata rather than a Resource-local instance rule.
No local Resource element has a fixed value, pattern, or default value in either version.
No local Resource element declares `minValue`, `maxValue`, `maxLength`, or a Resource-local regex limit in either version.
`Resource.implicitRules` remains `isModifier=true`; the root, `id`, `meta`, and `language` remain non-modifier elements.
`Resource.id`, `Resource.meta`, and `Resource.implicitRules` remain summary elements; root and `Resource.language` remain non-summary.
No slicing is declared on local Resource elements in either StructureDefinition.

No R6 local Resource element was added or given a new choice/reference type that cannot be represented in R4. R6 language codes remain string `code` values in R4, though old R4 tooling may treat non-Common-Languages BCP-47 tags as preferred-binding warnings.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Resource.implicitRules definition now references additionalImplicitRules for DomainResources
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `Resource.implicitRules` keeps the same path, cardinality `0..1`, type `uri`, modifier flag, and summary flag. The added text points readers to an extension for multiple implicit-rules policies on DomainResources, but does not change the base element shape.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Systems that interpret multiple implicit-rules policies should review the separate `additionalImplicitRules` extension and DomainResource behavior, but no direct Resource wire transform is required by this text change.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Common Languages is retained as a larger starter value set
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The local R6 Common Languages compose contains 93 concepts compared with 56 in R4, with no removed concepts in the local list comparison. In R6 this value set is only an additional starter binding for `Resource.language`; the conformance-limiting binding is the required All Languages value set.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Do not generate a closed enum from Common Languages for R6 `Resource.language`; use BCP-47 validation and treat Common Languages as a UI starter list.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 explicitly records mustSupport=false on local Resource elements
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 omits `mustSupport` on these base elements while R6 explicitly sets `mustSupport=false`. This is equivalent to the default false value and does not add a support obligation.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Definition consumers should normalize absent `mustSupport` to false when comparing R4 and R6.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Publisher/contact/jurisdiction and generated narrative metadata changed
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 adds generated narrative and jurisdiction metadata and updates publisher/contact details, but the canonical URL, name, kind, type, status, abstract flag, and local instance element set remain stable.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Package consumers should not treat narrative generation or publisher string changes as resource model breaks.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: The hard validation finding depends on how R6 terminology services validate `urn:ietf:bcp:47`, including private-use, grandfathered, script, and region subtags.
The `Resource.id` marker change should be reconciled with the primitive `id` datatype analysis and with code generators that map FHIR primitive subtypes.

R6 introduces an explicit `Base` StructureDefinition used as the superclass of Resource; broader cross-artifact hierarchy analysis should ensure derived resources and datatypes handle this consistently.
R6 `Resource.implicitRules` text references this extension for DomainResource multiple-policy cases. Its own compatibility and R4 mapping should be assessed outside the Resource base artifact.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The local ValueSet compose rules were compared, but no terminology server was used to validate the effective BCP-47 expansion. This limits precision about exactly which unusual tags will pass R6 required binding validation.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run R4 and R6 terminology validation examples against the intended production terminology server for BCP-47 tags.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official Resource R4-to-R6 diff page or change-note narrative was used. The analysis relies on local computable packages.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Compare against official published R4-to-R6 diff and Resource narrative pages when available.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 input is a ballot build (`6.0.0-ballot4`), not a final normative release. Findings describe this build and may change before final publication.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Re-run the comparison against the final R6 core package.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Runtime/code-generation impact was inferred from StructureDefinition metadata. No specific generated libraries, validators, or schemas were built and tested.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run representative R4 and R6 code generators and validators, then compare generated Resource inheritance and id property types.
